answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying reputation to costly, verifiable work instead of free identities. When agents must wander through a shared river of real tasks — staking small deposits, finishing jobs, and earning peer attestations over time — one operator cannot cheaply clone thousands of credible actors. Like shale layers that form only under sustained pressure, trust should build slowly and reset when an agent misbehaves, so fresh identities stay expensive while honest history stays valuable.
